title: Variational inequalities and spatial contact discretization

items.title: Partial-trace displacement space on a polygon
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. A **bounded connected Lipschitz polygon** $Ω\subset\mathbb R^2$ is a bounded connected open set whose boundary is a simple closed polygonal curve and, near every boundary point after a rigid coordinate change, is the graph of a Lipschitz function with $Ω$ on one side. Assume $Ω$ is a $W^{1,2}$-extension domain in the sense of [[def-sobolev-extension-domain-and-extension-operator]]. Fix two disjoint closed straight segments $Γ_D,Γ_C\subset\partialΩ$, each of positive length and each lying strictly inside a straight side of $∂Ω$.

As part of the geometry data, fix bounded $C^1$ subdomains $U_D,U_C\subsetΩ$ (in the sense of [[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]]) whose boundaries have relatively open flat patches containing $Γ_D,Γ_C$, respectively. Such collars can be chosen as sufficiently thin stadium-shaped domains along slightly longer segments of the same polygon sides, with their rounded ends outside the prescribed segments. Let $T_D,T_C$ be the restrictions to these segments of the bounded trace operators on $U_D,U_C$ supplied by [[thm-lp-trace-operator-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]], applied componentwise to the restrictions of functions in $H^1(Ω;\mathbb R^2)$. For $j\in\{D,C\}$, if $v\in H^1(Ω;\mathbb R^2)$ has a representative on $U_j$ extending continuously to $\overline{U_j}$, then $T_jv$ agrees in $L^2(Γ_j;\mathbb R^2)$ with that extension's restriction to $Γ_j$, by the trace theorem's agreement clause. In particular, this holds for $v\in H^1(Ω;\mathbb R^2)\cap C(\overlineΩ;\mathbb R^2)$.

Define
$$V:=\{v\in H^1(Ω;\mathbb R^2):T_Dv=0\text{ in }L^2(Γ_D;\mathbb R^2)\},\qquad \|v\|_V:=\|v\|_{H^1(Ω)}.$$
The contact normal $n\in\mathbb R^2$ is a fixed unit vector on $Γ_C$, oriented so that a positive value of $T_Cv\cdot n$ opens the contact gap. No pointwise value of a general $H^1$ class is used in this definition.
items.strategy: Use bounded C1 collars around the straight segments to define bounded traces, then define the zero-trace kernel.
items.axiom_base: Axiom of Choice is inherited from the bounded C1 trace theorem.

items.title: The partial-trace displacement space is a Hilbert space
items.statement: Assume the geometry and trace conventions of [[def-signorini-partial-trace-space]]. Then the maps $T_D,T_C:H^1(Ω;\mathbb R^2)\to L^2(Γ_D;\mathbb R^2),L^2(Γ_C;\mathbb R^2)$ are bounded and linear, and $V=\ker T_D$ is a Hilbert space with the inherited $H^1$ inner product.
items.strategy: Restrict to fixed C1 collars, apply the trace bound, and take the kernel of a bounded map.
items.axiom_base: Axiom of Choice is inherited from the trace theorem.

items.title: A planar rigid motion is controlled by its trace on a segment
items.statement:
Let $\Gamma_D$ be a fixed straight segment of length $L>0$ in the geometry of [[def-signorini-partial-trace-space]]. For every planar infinitesimal rigid motion $r(x)=a+\omega Jx$, where $a\in\mathbb R^2$, $\omega\in\mathbb R$, and $J=\begin{pmatrix}0&-1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$, there is a constant $C=C(\Omega,\Gamma_D)$ such that
$$\|r\|_{H^1(\Omega)}\le C\|T_Dr\|_{L^2(\Gamma_D)}.$$
items.strategy: Parameterize the segment and integrate the affine rigid-motion trace explicitly.
items.axiom_base: No choice principle is used in the local finite-dimensional estimate.

references.title: Jean-Luc Guermond, MATH 661 Fall 2025, Part XI Chapter 53: Stokes equations: Basic ideas

items.title: Small-strain elasticity with a frictionless contact gap
items.statement:
Use the polygon, displacement space and oriented contact normal from [[def-signorini-partial-trace-space]]. Let the constant shear modulus satisfy $\mu>0$, let the finite Lam\'e parameter satisfy $\lambda\ge0$, and let $F:V\to\mathbb R$ be a bounded linear functional. For $v\in V$, define the weak symmetric gradient
$$\varepsilon(v):=\frac{\nabla v+(\nabla v)^T}{2}.$$
For $u,v\in V$, define the isotropic small-strain elasticity form
$$a(u,v):=\int_\Omega 2\mu\,\varepsilon(u):\varepsilon(v)+\lambda\,\operatorname{div}u\,\operatorname{div}v\,dx.$$
The strain and form conventions are the algebraic formulas in [[def-linear-elasticity-displacement-formulation-and-data]]. The present domain is the partial-trace space $V$; all coercivity and well-posedness claims for it are proved locally below.
items.strategy: State the strain, stress-form bilinear energy, load space, normal orientation, and gap convention; import only the literal elasticity formula.
items.axiom_base: The definition uses no choice principle.

references.title: Jean-Luc Guermond, MATH 661 Fall 2025, Part XI Chapter 53: Stokes equations: Basic ideas
references.locator: §§53.1–53.2.1, printed pp. 391–394: the symmetric-gradient stress convention and weak formulation on a positive-measure Dirichlet velocity space. The elasticity energy form is cited to Zulehner below.

references.locator: Chapter 2 §2.1, printed pp. 20–22: displacement spaces and the linear-elasticity energy form.

items.title: The vector Signorini contact set and variational inequality
items.statement:
Let $\psi\in C(\Gamma_C;\mathbb R)$ satisfy $\psi\le0$. Define the unilateral frictionless **contact set**
$$K:=\{v\in V:T_Cv\cdot n\ge\psi\quad\text{for arclength-almost every point of }\Gamma_C\}.$$
Given the elasticity form $a$ and bounded load $F$ of [[def-signorini-elasticity-contact-model]], the **contact variational inequality** is to find $u\in K$ such that
$$a(u,v-u)\ge F(v-u)\qquad\text{for every }v\in K.$$
The set $K$ is nonempty, closed and convex by [[lem-signorini-contact-set-closed-convex-nonempty]].
items.strategy: Define the vector boundary gap and its variational inequality on the actual partial-trace displacement space.
items.axiom_base: The definition itself uses no choice principle; well-posedness is established separately.

items.title: The isotropic contact elasticity form is well defined and bounded
items.statement:
In the setting of [[def-signorini-elasticity-contact-model]], the form $a$ is well defined, symmetric, and satisfies
$$|a(u,v)|\le(2\mu+2\lambda)\|u\|_{H^1(\Omega)}\|v\|_{H^1(\Omega)}\qquad(u,v\in V).$$
items.strategy: Apply Cauchy-Schwarz to the strain and divergence terms and bound both by the full gradient.
items.axiom_base: No choice principle is used by the local L2 estimates.

items.title: The Signorini contact set is nonempty, closed, and convex
items.statement: Under [[def-signorini-contact-variational-inequality]], $K$ is nonempty, closed, and convex in the Hilbert space $V$.
items.strategy: Use continuity of the contact trace and closedness of the nonnegative cone in L2.
items.axiom_base: No choice principle is used beyond the inherited function-space interfaces.

items.title: Conforming nodal P1 Signorini contact discretization
items.statement:
Let $(\mathcal T_h)$ be a family of matching, boundary-conforming, shape-regular affine triangular meshes of the polygon from [[def-signorini-partial-trace-space]], with $h:=\max_{K\in\mathcal T_h}\operatorname{diam}(K)$. Assume both $\Gamma_D$ and $\Gamma_C$ are unions of boundary edges of each mesh, and let $\mathcal N_h^C$ be the vertices on $\Gamma_C$. The conforming continuous P1 displacement space is
$$V_h:=\{v_h\in V\cap C(\overline\Omega;\mathbb R^2):v_h|_K\in\mathbb P_1(K;\mathbb R^2)\text{ for every }K\in\mathcal T_h\}.$$
For continuous $\psi$ on $\Gamma_C$, let $I_h\psi$ be its continuous piecewise-affine nodal interpolant on the contact edges. Under the additional obstacle hypotheses $\psi\le0$ and convexity of $\psi$ in arclength on $\Gamma_C$, define
$$K_h:=\{v_h\in V_h:v_h(a)\cdot n\ge I_h\psi(a)\text{ for every }a\in\mathcal N_h^C\}.$$
The nodal inequalities are exactly the plan's vertex constraints. The well-definedness and conformity claims are proved in [[lem-signorini-nodal-contact-set-conforming]].
items.strategy: Specify the matching triangular mesh, global P1 displacement space, nodal obstacle interpolation, and exact constraint set.
items.axiom_base: The scheme definition uses no choice principle.

references.title: Richard S. Falk, Error Estimates for the Approximation of a Class of Variational Inequalities, complete 10-page paper
references.locator: §3, printed pp. 966–969: continuous P1 spaces, vertex obstacle constraints, and feasible interpolants.

references.title: Jean-Luc Guermond, MATH 661 Fall 2025, Chapter 11: Local interpolation on affine meshes

items.title: Korn coercivity with a partial Dirichlet segment
items.statement:
Assume the geometry of [[def-signorini-partial-trace-space]] and let $V=\{v\in H^1(\Omega;\mathbb R^2):T_Dv=0\}$. Then there is $c_K>0$, depending on $\Omega$ and $\Gamma_D$, such that
$$\|v\|_{H^1(\Omega)}\le c_K\|\varepsilon(v)\|_{L^2(\Omega)}\qquad(v\in V).$$
items.strategy: Subtract the rigid-motion component, use a zero-mean divergence lift to control the skew gradient by strain, then remove the rigid motion with the Dirichlet trace.
items.axiom_base: Countable Choice is used by the divergence right inverse; the Axiom of Choice is used by Poincare-Wirtinger compactness.

references.title: Walter Zulehner, Numerical Methods for Continuum Mechanics 1, complete 80-page lecture notes
references.locator: Chapter 2 §2.1, printed pp. 22–23: Lemma 2.2 states second Korn in dimension d; Corollary 2.1 states positive-measure Dirichlet coercivity in three dimensions.

references.title: Jean-Luc Guermond, MATH 661 Fall 2025, Part XI Chapter 53: Stokes equations: Basic ideas
references.locator: §53.2, printed pp. 393–395: the positive-measure Dirichlet velocity space and coercivity of its symmetric-gradient form via Korn's inequality.

items.title: The convex-obstacle nodal set is conforming
items.statement: Under [[def-signorini-nodal-p1-contact-scheme]], $K_h$ is a nonempty closed convex subset of the finite-dimensional space $V_h$ and $K_h\subseteq K$. If $v\in K\cap H^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^2)\cap C(\overline\Omega;\mathbb R^2)$, its global P1 nodal interpolant $I_hv$ is well defined, belongs to $V_h$, and lies in $K_h$.
items.strategy: Check zero feasibility and finite-dimensional halfspaces, then compare affine edge gaps with convex obstacle chords.
items.axiom_base: No additional choice principle is used.

references.title: John Andersson, The Obstacle Problem, complete 52-page KTH lecture notes
references.locator: Chapter 3 §3.1, printed pp. 26–28: continuous obstacle feasible sets and their minimizers.

items.title: Contact nodal coordinates are independently attainable
items.statement: Under [[def-signorini-nodal-p1-contact-scheme]], let the contact vertices be $a_0,\ldots,a_N$ and define $B:V_h\to\mathbb R^{N+1}$ by $B_i(v_h)=v_h(a_i)\cdot n$. Then $B$ is onto. In particular, for each $i$ there is $w_i\in V_h$ with $B_j(w_i)=\delta_{ij}$ for every contact vertex $a_j$.
items.strategy: Construct the global P1 nodal function from local affine barycentric coordinates, prove matching traces and zero Dirichlet trace, and evaluate its contact coordinates.
items.axiom_base: The finite barycentric construction is choice-free; the trace interface inherits the Axiom of Choice.

references.title: Richard S. Falk, Error Estimates for the Approximation of a Class of Variational Inequalities, complete 10-page paper
references.locator: §3, printed pp. 966–970: conforming P1 spaces and vertex degrees of freedom.

references.title: Jean-Luc Guermond, MATH 661 Fall 2025, Chapter 11: Local interpolation on affine meshes
references.locator: §§11.1 and 11.5.1, printed pp. 118–128: affine triangles and the Lagrange nodal basis.

items.title: Dual P1 mortar multipliers for boundary contact
items.statement:
On a contact mesh with nodes $a_0,\ldots,a_N$ and edges $e_k=[a_k,a_{k+1}]$ of lengths $h_k>0$, let $W_h$ be the continuous piecewise-affine scalar trace space with nodal basis $\phi_0,\ldots,\phi_N$. On $e_k$, write the local endpoint basis as $\phi_k^{e_k},\phi_{k+1}^{e_k}$. Define broken piecewise-affine dual functions by
$$\chi_i|_{e_k}=\begin{cases}4\phi_k^{e_k}-2\phi_{k+1}^{e_k},&i=k,\\-2\phi_k^{e_k}+4\phi_{k+1}^{e_k},&i=k+1,\\0,&i\notin\{k,k+1\},\end{cases}$$
and set $\Lambda_h:=\operatorname{span}\{\chi_i:0\le i\le N\}\subset L^2(\Gamma_C)$. The **positive discrete multiplier cone** is
$$\Lambda_h^+:=\left\{\lambda_h=\sum_{i=0}^N\lambda_i\chi_i:\lambda_i\ge0\right\}.$$
The functions $\chi_i$ have support on the one or two contact edges incident to $a_i$ and can jump at contact nodes. For $v_h\in V_h$ and $\lambda_h\in\Lambda_h$, define the exact mortar coupling
$$b_h(v_h,\lambda_h):=\int_{\Gamma_C}\lambda_h\,T_Cv_h\cdot n\,ds.$$
The cone $\Lambda_h^+$ is coefficientwise; its elements need not be pointwise nonnegative. Its dual-cone and stability properties are proved in [[lem-signorini-dual-mortar-biorthogonality-and-infsup]]. This is a matching boundary mortar pair and makes no nonmatching-interface claim.
items.strategy: Define the local two-node L2-dual basis, its assembled multiplier space, and the coefficientwise positive cone.
items.axiom_base: No choice principle is used by the finite-dimensional construction.

references.title: Rolf H. Krause and Barbara I. Wohlmuth, Multigrid Methods for Mortar Finite Elements, complete 7-page paper
references.locator: §2, printed pp. 2–3: dual P1 mortar multiplier functions and biorthogonality.

items.title: Continuous frictionless elasticity contact is well posed
items.statement:
Assume the setting of [[def-signorini-contact-variational-inequality]], including the Axiom of Choice for the trace/Poincare interfaces and Countable Choice. For every bounded linear load $F:V\to\mathbb R$, there is exactly one $u\in K$ satisfying the contact variational inequality. With $\alpha:=2\mu/c_K^2$, where $c_K$ is from [[lem-signorini-partial-dirichlet-korn-coercivity]], solutions for two loads $F_1,F_2$ satisfy
$$\alpha\|u_1-u_2\|_V\le\|F_1-F_2\|_{V^*}.$$
items.strategy: Prove boundedness and coercivity of the elasticity form, apply Stampacchia, and then apply the literal load-stability estimate.
items.axiom_base: Countable Choice is used by Stampacchia and its stability theorem; the Korn supplier also carries its declared Axiom of Choice branch.

references.title: John Andersson, The Obstacle Problem, complete 52-page KTH lecture notes
references.locator: Chapter 3 §3.1, Theorem 3.1 and printed pp. 26–28: closed convex obstacle sets and variational inequalities.

references.title: Richard S. Falk, Error Estimates for the Approximation of a Class of Variational Inequalities, complete 10-page paper
references.locator: §2, Theorem 1, printed p. 965: a general approximation error estimate for coercive variational inequalities. The introduction attributes existence and uniqueness to Lions–Stampacchia.

items.title: The dual mortar basis is biorthogonal and uniformly stable on the trace space
items.statement:
For the spaces and basis of [[def-signorini-dual-mortar-contact-pair]], put $d_i:=\sum_{e_k\ni a_i}h_k$. Then
$$\int_{\Gamma_C}\chi_i\phi_j\,ds=d_i\delta_{ij}\qquad(0\le i,j\le N).$$
The pair $(\Lambda_h,W_h)$ satisfies the mesh-independent trace-space inf-sup bound
$$\inf_{0\ne\lambda_h\in\Lambda_h}\sup_{0\ne g_h\in W_h}\frac{\int_{\Gamma_C}\lambda_hg_h\,ds}{\|\lambda_h\|_{L^2(\Gamma_C)}\|g_h\|_{L^2(\Gamma_C)}}\ge\frac1{\sqrt3}.$$
Moreover, $\lambda_h\in\Lambda_h^+$ defines a nonnegative functional on the cone of nonnegative functions in $W_h$, and $\langle\lambda_h,g_h\rangle=\sum_i d_i\lambda_i g_h(a_i)$.
items.strategy: Compute the two-by-two reference mass matrix on each edge, assemble its diagonal dual pairings, and use local norm equivalence.
items.axiom_base: No choice principle is used; all matrices and sums are finite.

references.title: Rolf H. Krause and Barbara I. Wohlmuth, Multigrid Methods for Mortar Finite Elements, complete 7-page paper
references.locator: §2, printed pp. 2–3: local dual basis, biorthogonality, and diagonal mass pairing.

items.title: Falk error bound for nodal Signorini contact
items.statement:
Assume the contact model and nodal scheme above, with $K_h\subseteq K$, the exact restrictions of $a,F$ to $V_h$, and shape-regular boundary-conforming meshes. Let $u\in K$ and $u_h\in K_h$ solve their continuous and discrete variational inequalities, respectively. Put $\alpha=2\mu/c_K^2$, $M=2\mu+2\lambda$, and
$$\eta_{\rm feas}(v_h):=a(u,v_h-u)-F(v_h-u)\quad(v_h\in K_h).$$
Then $\eta_{\rm feas}(v_h)\ge0$ and
$$\|u-u_h\|_V^2\le\inf_{v_h\in K_h}\left\{\frac{M^2}{\alpha^2}\|u-v_h\|_V^2+\frac{2}{\alpha}\eta_{\rm feas}(v_h)\right\}.$$
The term $\eta_{\rm feas}$ is the explicit feasible-comparison defect; the form and load have no quadrature or geometry perturbation here. If additionally $u\in H^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^2)\cap C(\overline\Omega;\mathbb R^2)$, the obstacle is convex as required by [[def-signorini-nodal-p1-contact-scheme]], the meshes are uniformly shape regular with $h\to0$, then $I_hu\in K_h$, $\|u-I_hu\|_V\to0$, $\eta_{\rm feas}(I_hu)\to0$, and consequently $u_h\to u$ in $V$.
items.strategy: Test the continuous and discrete inequalities at feasible comparison points, apply Young's inequality, and use the local P1 H2 interpolation estimate for the conditional convergence branch.
items.axiom_base: Countable Choice is used for discrete Stampacchia existence; Lagrange nodal boundedness and the interpolation supplier use the Axiom of Choice.

references.title: Richard S. Falk, Error Estimates for the Approximation of a Class of Variational Inequalities, complete 10-page paper
references.locator: §2, Theorem 1, printed pp. 964–965, and §3, Lemma 3, printed pp. 969–970: feasible-set defects and nodal comparisons.

references.title: Jean-Luc Guermond, MATH 661 Fall 2025, Chapter 11: Local interpolation on affine meshes
references.locator: §§11.2, 11.4 and 11.5.1, printed pp. 120–128: affine scaling, the complete local interpolation theorem, and its Lagrange-element application.

items.title: The dual mortar contact system is stable and exactly complementary
items.statement:
On each fixed contact mesh in [[def-signorini-dual-mortar-contact-pair]], assume $K_h\subseteq K$, the elasticity form is bounded and coercive on $V_h$ with constants $M,\alpha>0$, and $F$ is bounded. Then the nodal contact variational inequality has a unique displacement $u_h$ and a unique multiplier $\lambda_h=\sum_i\lambda_i\chi_i\in\Lambda_h^+$ satisfying
$$a(u_h,v_h)-F(v_h)=b_h(v_h,\lambda_h)\quad(v_h\in V_h),$$
$$g_i:=u_h(a_i)\cdot n-I_h\psi(a_i)\ge0,\quad \lambda_i\ge0,\quad \lambda_i g_i=0\quad(0\le i\le N).$$
These saddle equations are equivalent to the discrete VI, and the integrated complementarity residual is exactly $\mathcal R_h:=\int_{\Gamma_C}\lambda_h(T_Cu_h\cdot n-I_h\psi)\,ds=\sum_i d_i\lambda_i g_i=0$. The trace-pair inf-sup bound is at least $1/\sqrt3$ in the stated $L^2$ norms by [[lem-signorini-dual-mortar-biorthogonality-and-infsup]], and the displacement satisfies $\|u_h\|_V\le\|F\|_{V^*}/\alpha$. The coupling uses exact edge integrals and has no contact quadrature defect.
items.strategy: Use coercive finite-dimensional VI existence, prove the nodal constraint map is onto, derive complementary multipliers from feasible coordinate variations, and use biorthogonality for exact consistency.
items.axiom_base: Countable Choice is inherited from the discrete Stampacchia theorem.

references.title: Rolf H. Krause and Barbara I. Wohlmuth, Multigrid Methods for Mortar Finite Elements, complete 7-page paper
references.locator: §2, printed pp. 2–3: dual multiplier basis, biorthogonality, and equivalent mortar saddle formulation.

title: Variational inequalities and spatial contact discretization — Examples

items.title: A one-dimensional obstacle with an explicit free boundary
items.statement:
On $(0,1)$ take $a_0=1/2$, obstacle $\psi(x)=0$ for $0\le x\le a_0$ and $\psi(x)=-(x-a_0)$ for $a_0\le x\le1$, bilinear form $a(w,z)=\int_0^1w'z'\,dx$, and load $F(z)=\int_0^1f z\,dx$, where
$$u(x)=\begin{cases}0,&0\le x\le a_0,\\(x-a_0)^2(1-x),&a_0\le x\le1,\end{cases}\qquad f(x)=\begin{cases}-1,&0<x<a_0,\\-4+6x,&a_0<x<1.\end{cases}$$
Then $u$ is the unique solution of the scalar obstacle variational inequality. Using the displayed continuous representatives on $[0,1]$, their coincidence set on $\overline\Omega$ is $[0,a_0]$; the contact set within $\Omega=(0,1)$ is $(0,a_0]$. The reaction density is $1$ on $(0,a_0)$ and $0$ on $(a_0,1)$.
items.strategy: Verify endpoint traces, obstacle feasibility, the piecewise weak residual, and uniqueness by the published scalar VI theorem.
items.axiom_base: Axiom of Choice is required by the imported scalar obstacle definition; Countable Choice is used by Stampacchia existence and uniqueness.

references.title: John Andersson, The Obstacle Problem, complete 52-page KTH lecture notes
references.locator: Chapter 3 §3.1, Theorem 3.1, printed p. 27: existence and uniqueness for the scalar Dirichlet obstacle problem; printed pp. 27–28 derive its variational inequality by admissible variations. The reaction density in this example is computed locally.

references.title: Richard S. Falk, Error Estimates for the Approximation of a Class of Variational Inequalities, complete 10-page paper
references.locator: §2, Theorem 1, printed pp. 964–965: coercive obstacle variational inequalities.

items.title: Nodal feasibility can miss a nonconvex obstacle between vertices
items.statement: Let $\Omega=(0,1)^2$, $\Gamma_D=\{0\}\times[1/4,3/4]$, $\Gamma_C=\{1\}\times[1/4,3/4]$, and $n=(1,0)$. Use the grid $x\in\{0,1/2,1\}$, $y\in\{0,1/4,3/4,1\}$ and split each rectangular cell by a diagonal. This is a matching triangular mesh on which both segments are single boundary edges. Parameterize $\Gamma_C$ by normalized arclength $s=2(y-1/4)\in[0,1]$, set $\psi(s)=-1+4s(1-s)$, and let $v_h(x,y)=(-x,0)$. The obstacle is continuous, nonpositive and concave, and $v_h$ satisfies both endpoint nodal inequalities, but $v_h\notin K$ because its contact gap is negative at the midpoint.
items.strategy: Give a concave nonpositive obstacle and an affine gap that meets the endpoint constraints but violates the midpoint constraint.
items.axiom_base: No choice principle is used.

references.title: Richard S. Falk, Error Estimates for the Approximation of a Class of Variational Inequalities, complete 10-page paper
references.locator: §3, printed pp. 966–970: nodal obstacle constraints and the need to control the between-node obstacle comparison.

items.title: An affine shear field passes the frictionless contact patch test
items.statement: On the unit square with $\Gamma_D=\{0\}\times[1/4,3/4]$, $\Gamma_C=\{1\}\times[1/4,3/4]$, and $n=(1,0)$, use any matching boundary-conforming affine triangular mesh that resolves both segments as unions of boundary edges, and take obstacle $\psi=0$. Let $u(x,y)=(0,x)$ and define the load $F(v)=a(u,v)$ on $V$. Then $u$ is the unique continuous solution and, on every such mesh, the same field is the unique nodal P1 solution. Its contact gap is identically zero.
items.strategy: Compute strain/divergence and use F(v)=a(u,v) to verify exact equality in both the continuous and discrete inequalities.
items.axiom_base: The verification is an exact finite-dimensional and affine calculation.

references.title: Jean-Luc Guermond, MATH 661 Fall 2025, Part XI Chapter 53: Stokes equations: Basic ideas

items.title: A two-gap contact model changes its active set with the load
items.statement: Consider the reduced two-gap variational inequality with stiffness $A=\begin{pmatrix}2&-1\\-1&2\end{pmatrix}$: for a load $f\in\mathbb R^2$, find $g\in\mathbb R_+^2$ such that $(Ag-f)\cdot(z-g)\ge0$ for every $z\in\mathbb R_+^2$. Its complementarity form is $Ag-f=\rho$, $g_i\ge0$, $\rho_i\ge0$, and $\rho_i g_i=0$. The scaling $\rho_i=d_i\lambda_i$ matches [[thm-signorini-mortar-contact-kkt-and-complementarity]], where $d_i>0$ is the diagonal dual-pair weight and $\lambda_i$ is the multiplier coefficient. For $f^{(1)}=(1,1/5)^T$, both gaps are positive and no constraint is active. For $f^{(2)}=(1,-1)^T$, the second constraint alone is active, with $g=(1/2,0)^T$ and $\rho=(0,1/2)^T$. This is an algebraic reduced model; the chosen matrix is not asserted to arise from a particular geometric mesh.
items.strategy: Solve the two finite KKT systems directly and verify feasibility, stationarity, multiplier signs, and complementarity.
items.axiom_base: No choice principle is used in the finite calculation.
